instruction: Create an Ubuntu user named 'emma' with the password 'T3mpP@ss!', assign '/home/test1' as the home directory, and ensure the password expires in 30 days.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a user 'emma' with password 'T3mpP@ss!' that expires in 30 days, with home directory /home/test1. The evaluator comprehensively checks all 4 requirements: (1) user 'emma' exists, (2) home directory is /home/test1, (3) password authentication capability, and (4) password expiry is 30 days. Custom getter get_user_passwd_expiry__9c1a98b9ab77ed8338363ad0c57d51e2 retrieves user existence, home directory, password authentication status, and password max days. Custom metric check_passwd_expiry__9c1a98b9ab77ed8338363ad0c57d51e2 verifies all requirements with partial credit (0.25 per requirement) for a total score of 0.0-1.0.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator correctly checks all 4 instruction requirements: (1) user 'emma' exists, (2) home directory is '/home/test1', (3) password authentication capability, (4) password expiry is 30 days
User existence verified: Getter uses 'getent passwd emma' to check if user exists (os_user.py:35-49), returns user_exists=True/False
Home directory verified: Getter parses passwd entry to extract home directory (os_user.py:43-45), metric compares to expected '/home/test1' (os_user.py:40-53)
Password expiry verified correctly: Getter extracts max days via 'chage -l' command (os_user.py:55-63), metric compares to expected '30' (os_user.py:65-77)
Partial credit logic is sound: Metric awards 0.25 per requirement with early exit if user doesn't exist (os_user.py:30-80)
Expected parameter handling is correct: Metric properly accesses expected.get('max_days') and expected.get('home_directory') directly when type='rule'

Minor limitation: password_auth_works is set to True unconditionally if user exists (os_user.py:69-70) without actually verifying password 'T3mpP@ss!'. Comment acknowledges this limitation (os_user.py:65-68). Postconfig installs 'expect' tool suggesting password testing was considered but deemed too complex
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider implementing actual password verification using 'expect' tool (already installed in postconfig). Could test login with provided password 'T3mpP@ss!' to verify it was set correctly, though this adds complexity
